source.title: Steering Large Language Model Activations in Sparse Spaces
source.authors: Reza Bayat; Ali Rahimi-Kalahroudi; Mohammad Pezeshki; A. P. Sarath Chandar; Pascal Vincent

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses superposition and SAE feature disentanglement as motivation for a new activation-steering method, then reports how that method performs. It does not measure whether individual neurons have multiple unrelated jobs.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition as background and measures sparsity and overlap of SAE steering features, not individual-neuron selectivity or polysemanticity. Those feature-space results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The behavioral changes caused by deliberately applying steering vectors do not establish how often the behaviors or features occur without intervention. Cited results from other work and values used only to choose settings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper invokes superposition as background and proposes an SAE-based steering method; it reports steering performance and SAS-vector sparsity, never measuring whether individual model neurons respond to unrelated inputs, how common that is, or what causes it.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: SAS enables interpretable, compositional steering with little benchmark cost, and scaling SAEs makes SAS vectors sparser (termed monosemanticity). No conclusions about individual-neuron polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: The study builds SAS vectors from contrastive prompts in SAE feature space and steers activations; it does not use the original studies' neuron-level visualization or SoLU methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SAS-vector sparsity varies with SAE width and tau; steering outcomes also vary with steering strength, layer, and direction. The paper reports stable positive-steering performance and some negative-steering degradation at higher tau in the SAE-scaling experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger SAE widths (16K to 1M) give fewer active features in contrastive SAS steering vectors, while raw active-feature counts stay stable and positive steering performance is maintained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider SAE dictionaries yield sparser behavior-specific steering vectors without large loss in steering effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature overlap across behavior SAS vectors is lower at 1M width than 65K width (e.g. diagonal AI Coordination 127 vs 121, Refusal 113 vs 92).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider SAEs reduce shared features among behavioral steering vectors.

record.problems: The SAE-scaling results are primarily shown in figures without tabulated values or reported uncertainty. The authors acknowledge that SAE features are not guaranteed to be fully monosemantic. The experiments measure sparse feature vectors and steering performance, not individual-neuron polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; five related-result rows are recorded.

untested.parts: All; superposition only cited as background.

record.verdict_notes: Gemma-2 2B/9B instruction-tuned with Gemma Scope SAEs. The word 'monosemanticity' refers to steering-vector sparsity, not neurons; no row bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Vision-model neuron responses and the InceptionV1 example.
The share of polysemantic MLP neurons in language models and layer differences in neuron responses.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than available neurons.
Polysemantic neurons arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and whether it can be reduced without large performance loss.
Whether canonical mixed-response neurons detect a shared feature or related jobs rather than unrelated inputs.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Varied SAE dictionary width and measured the number of active features in SAS vectors.
rows.measure: Number of active features in SAS vectors
rows.note: The text says increasing SAE width reduces active SAS-vector features, particularly at higher tau, and interprets this as improved monosemanticity. This is a measure of SAE steering vectors, not individual neurons.
rows.check: Measures active SAE features in the paper's own steering vectors versus SAE width; not neuron polysemanticity. 'Monosemanticity' here means SAS-vector sparsity.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Varied SAE dictionary width and measured active features in raw sparse activations.
rows.measure: Average number of active features in raw sparse activations from positive and negative completions
rows.note: The text states that the total number of raw active features remains stable across SAE widths. This measures sparse activations, not polysemantic neuron prevalence.
rows.check: Raw SAE feature counts, not neuron-level selectivity.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated positive SAS steering across SAE dictionary widths on multiple-choice questions.
rows.note: The authors describe positive-steering performance as stable across SAE scaling. This is a performance result for an induced intervention, not a measure of neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Performance of the study's own induced steering method; arguably should not be a claim row.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated negative SAS steering across SAE dictionary widths on multiple-choice questions.
rows.note: The authors describe minor degradation for negative steering at higher tau. This is a performance result for an induced intervention, not a measure of neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Performance of the study's own induced steering method; arguably should not be a claim row.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared feature overlap among SAS behavior vectors at two SAE widths.
rows.measure: Overlap of features across behavior steering vectors
rows.value: 1M SAE: fewer total overlapping features, as described by the authors
rows.note: The paper attributes fewer observed features at 1M width to increased sparsity and improved disentanglement. These are SAE feature overlaps, not neuron response mixtures.
rows.check: SAE feature overlap between steering vectors; numbers are readable from Figures 24-25 but not neuron-level.
